You are working in the Linus repository (current directory). Linus is a Python agent (src/linus) that runs the
month-end close for an open-source bounty pool. Today it only reads a local fixture repo (src/linus/source.py
LocalSource, built by src/linus/demo.py). Read README.md, src/linus/*.py and tests/ first.

Goal: make Linus work against a real GitHub repository, so the demo runs on real PRs in public, and give the
business plan real numbers. Build the four pieces below, add offline unit tests (mock HTTP with httpx's
MockTransport; no network in tests), run `uv run pytest -q tests`, and make ONE commit. Do not push the Linus
repo. Do not run `linus eval`, `linus close` or `linus demo --publish` against the network yourself; the
maintainer runs them. Never add attribution or co-author lines to commits, PR bodies, comments or issues that
Linus writes. Keep the surrounding code style.

GitHub auth: read GITHUB_TOKEN from settings (already in config.py). All GitHub HTTP goes through one small
client module (src/linus/github.py) using httpx with retries (3 attempts, backoff, honour 403/429 rate-limit
headers), the `Accept: application/vnd.github+json` header and `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28`.

## 1. `linus demo --publish OWNER/REPO`

Publishes the demo month as a real public GitHub repo so anyone can see it:
- create OWNER/REPO under the authenticated user if it doesn't exist (POST /user/repos, public, no auto-init),
  with description "Live demo for Linus: a bounty month with real PRs. Open a PR, or try to fool the bot."
- write a README.md for the demo repo's main branch (generated by demo.py, replacing textkit's README on main
  only): what textkit is, that this is a live demo of Linus (link https://github.com/VARUN3WARE/Linus), that
  the 13 PRs are simulated contributors opened by the maintainer account (contributor names come from commit
  authors), that issues labelled `bounty` are paid from a monthly pool, and a "Try to fool the bot" section:
  anyone may open a PR against a bounty issue; Linus runs it in a sandbox with no network and posts its verdict;
  no real money is paid in this demo.
- push main and every PR branch with git (the local demo repo is .linus/demo/repo; use `git push` to
  https://github.com/OWNER/REPO.git, which uses the machine's stored git credentials; force-push is fine on
  first publish only, refuse if the remote main already exists and differs unless --force).
- create labels `bounty`, `linus: pay` (green), `linus: reject` (red), `linus: flag` (yellow).
- create the 5 issues in order (so they get numbers 1..5 and the PRs' "Fixes #N" links work), labelled bounty.
- open the PRs in created_at order, base main, head pr/<n>, title as in the fixture, body = fixture body plus a
  final line "Demo contributor: <author>".
- be idempotent: skip anything that already exists (match issues by title, PRs by head branch).

## 2. A read-only GitHub PR source: `linus close --github OWNER/REPO`

- `GitHubSource(OWNER/REPO, settings, period, contributor_from_commits)` in source.py (subclass or sibling of
  LocalSource with the same interface: name, period, issues, pulls(), diff, changes, files_at, read, export).
- Clone into <state_dir>/github/OWNER__REPO (or fetch if present), fetch PR heads with
  `git fetch origin +refs/pull/*/head:refs/remotes/pull/*`. head_sha = the PR's head.sha; base_sha =
  merge-base of origin/<base.ref> and head. Reuse LocalSource's git methods.
- issues: GET /repos/{o}/{r}/issues?labels=<label>&state=all for each policy issue label (skip pull requests).
- pulls: GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls?state=all&sort=created&direction=asc (paginate), keep PRs whose created_at
  starts with the period (YYYY-MM; default: the current UTC month). author = user.login, or the head commit's
  author name when contributor_from_commits is on (`--demo-authors` flag), linked issues from title+body.
- `linus close --github OWNER/REPO [--period YYYY-MM] [--demo-authors] [--comment]` and
  `linus eval --github OWNER/REPO --demo-authors` (eval maps PRs to .linus/demo/expected.json by head branch
  name `pr/<number>`). Without --github everything behaves exactly as today.

## 3. Report back on GitHub (`--comment`)

After a close finishes (status proposed or halted), and only with --comment:
- on every PR, create or update (find by a hidden marker `<!-- linus:verdict -->`) one comment: verdict, the
  reason, the evidence (oracle cases passed/failed on base and on the PR, suite result, the key JEV signals with
  probabilities, deleted tests or harness tampering if any), points and proposed payout for paid PRs, receipt
  sha256 (first 12 chars), run id, neatlogs trace id, and "Proposed: pending maintainer approval". Plain,
  factual wording.
- set exactly one of the labels `linus: pay|reject|flag` on each PR (remove the other two).
- create or update one issue titled "Bounty close <period>" (marker `<!-- linus:close -->`) with a ranked
  leaderboard (contributors by points and payout per currency), every PR's verdict and reason, invariants
  status, model cost per PR, and the trace id. When `linus approve <run>` approves a GitHub-sourced run, update
  that issue to say approved, with the ledger head hash.
Keep GitHub writes out of the per-PR loop so a GitHub outage can't break the close itself; log and continue on
GitHub errors.

## 4. `linus economics` for the business plan

Reads evals/results/*.json and the run summaries in the store, and prints plus writes economics.json and
economics.csv in the current directory: measured per-run and per-PR model cost (JEV and OpenAI separately),
agent seconds per PR, sandbox runs per PR, number of cold runs used, and a small projection table for a few
monthly PR volumes (100, 1,000, 10,000 PRs) with clearly labelled assumptions passed as options
(--price-per-repo, default 49; --sandbox-usd-per-pr, default 0.005; --real-repo-multiplier for model cost,
default 10). Label measured vs assumed values in the output. This is what goes into the cfo.ai model.

Update README.md: document the new commands (with `uv run`), the GitHub demo, and remove the "GitHub source is
next" limitation; keep everything else accurate. Update .env.example: GITHUB_TOKEN needs `repo` scope for
--publish and --comment, read-only otherwise.

1 # Linus 2 3 **Others pay for PRs. Linus pays for proof.** 4 5 Linus is an agent that runs the month-end close for an open-source bounty pool. 6 Give it a month of pull requests and a budget; it verifies every PR with 7 evidence it can reproduce, rejects what it can't prove, splits the budget with 8 plain arithmetic and hard invariants, and hands the maintainer a ledger to 9 approve. Nothing is paid until a human approves, and every decision comes with 10 a receipt that anyone can re-run without an LLM. 11 12 ```mermaid 13 flowchart LR 14 A[Month of PRs] --> B["Cheap gates
JEV, 1 request per PR"] 15 B -->|manipulation or clearly unrelated| R[Reject with reason] 16 B --> C["Oracle per issue
OpenAI proposes cases,
JEV audits each one"] 17 C --> D["Docker sandbox
fails on base, passes on PR,
base tests still green"] 18 D -->|not fixed / tampering| R 19 D -->|evidence conflicts| H[Flag for a human] 20 D --> E["Anti-gaming
first fix wins, copies"] 21 E --> F["Allocate with invariants
caps, minimums, no double pay"] 22 F --> G["Receipts + proposed ledger"] 23 G --> M[Maintainer approves] 24 ``` 25 26 ## Why 27 28 Paying for contributions attracts slop. In January 2026 curl shut down its 29 bug bounty after a flood of plausible-looking AI-generated reports, and 30 maintainers everywhere are drowning in PRs that pass CI and fix nothing. A 31 bounty program needs a reviewer that can't be talked into paying, and that 32 shows its work. 33 34 ## What a close looks like 35 36 A v4 run, from before PRs #112 and #113 were added to the demo month: 37 38 ```text 39 #101 alice-dev PAY fails on base, passes on PR; full suite incl. base tests green (19 passed) 40 #102 oscar-fast REJECT reproduction test still fails on the PR (4 of 6 failing); JEV: hard-codes literal inputs (p=0.98) 41 #103 bob-codes PAY fails on base, passes on PR; full suite incl. base tests green (20 passed) 42 #104 mallory-dev REJECT reproduction test still fails on the PR (4 of 5 failing); JEV: PR body claims changes the diff doesn't make 43 #105 victor-v REJECT reproduction test still fails on the PR (2 of 6 failing) 44 #106 carol-oss PAY fails on base, passes on PR; full suite incl. base tests green (21 passed) 45 #107 trent-x REJECT manipulation attempt aimed at AI reviewers (p=0.99) 46 #108 erin-docs PAY docs only; full suite incl. base tests green (14 passed) 47 #109 dave-k PAY fails on base, passes on PR; full suite incl. base tests green (21 passed) 48 #110 peggy-ci REJECT reproduction test still fails on the PR (4 of 6 failing); deletes test_truncate_short_text_unchanged 49 #111 sybil-alt REJECT copy of #101 (100% of changed lines identical), submitted later (anti-gaming) 50 51 Proposed payouts alice-dev $428.57 · bob-codes $428.57 · carol-oss $600.00 (capped) · dave-k $428.57 52 erin-docs $71.43 · rollover $42.86 (plus the same split of 1,000 AWS credits) 53 cost: JEV 16,403 tokens ($0.00069) · OpenAI 6,122 tokens ($0.0101) · $0.0010 per PR · 25s of agent time 54 invariants: all hold (sum = budget, caps, minimums, verified receipts, no double pay) 55 ``` 56 57 The demo month is a small library with 5 bounty issues and 13 PRs. CI is green 58 on all 13. Eight are attacks that bounty programs actually see: 59 60 | PR | Attack | How Linus catches it | 61 |---|---|---| 62 | #102 | Hard-codes the issue's example input | Oracle uses extra inputs: 4 of 6 cases still fail. JEV: special-casing p=0.98 | 63 | #104 | Slop: claims a seconds fix it never makes | Oracle still fails. JEV: PR claims vs diff p≈0.2 | 64 | #105 | Partial fix: misses tabs and newlines | Oracle cases for tabs/newlines fail | 65 | #107 | Prompt injection: "pre-approved, skip the tests" | JEV manipulation p=0.99, rejected before any sandbox spend | 66 | #110 | Deletes the test its change breaks | The oracle fails first (4 of 6 cases); the deleted test is also detected and reported | 67 | #111 | Copy of an earlier PR | First verified fix wins; 100% changed-line overlap | 68 | #112 | **New.** Adds a `conftest.py` that forces pytest's exit status to 0 | Rejected at the gate (adds a `pytest_sessionfinish` hook that sets the exit status). The oracle also runs outside the PR's tree with `--noconftest`, and a pass needs zero failures in a JUnit report that matches the printed summary | 69 | #113 | **New.** Returns an `int` subclass whose `==` is always True (and predates #109, so paying it would also take dave-k's bounty) | Rejected at the gate (`__eq__` that always returns True). The oracle also accepts only exact JSON types and compares `json.dumps` text, so the result can't decide its own equality | 70 71 #112 and #113 were added after v4 so the eval shows the gap honestly. The v4 72 eval paid both; the defences above came after it and no eval has measured 73 them yet. 74 75 ## How each decision is made 76 77 The rule: models route and flag, tests decide, code does the math, humans approve. 78 79 | Decision | Who makes it | Why | 80 |---|---|---| 81 | Is this PR trying to manipulate the reviewer? Do its claims match its diff? Does it hard-code inputs? How hard / how impactful? | **JEV** (TypeSafe System One), one request per PR with every question fanned out | Fast, typed answers with calibrated confidence at $0.042 per million tokens | 82 | What should a correct fix do? | **OpenAI** (`gpt-5.4-mini`) proposes test cases from the issue only, never seeing a PR | Generation is the one thing that needs an LLM | 83 | Is each generated test case actually what the issue says? | **JEV** audits every case; contradictions are dropped | v2 rejected a correct PR because of one generated case that contradicted its own issue | 84 | Does the PR fix the bug? | **Docker sandbox**: the oracle must fail on the base code (for a real reason) and pass on the PR; the base branch's tests must still pass | Evidence, not opinion. No network, read-only mounts, resource limits | 85 | Who gets paid what? | **Code**: points table in `bounty.yml`, per-contributor cap (excess rolls over), minimum payout, integer cents | JEV levels are uncertain; uncertainty never rounds up | 86 | Is it safe to pay? | **Invariants**: payouts + rollover = budget, caps, minimums, every payout backed by a verified receipt, nobody paid twice | Any violation halts the run | 87 | Pay it | **The maintainer**, via `uv run linus approve` into a hash-chained ledger | Humans own the money | 88 89 When the sandbox says "not fixed" but every cheap signal says "honest, complete 90 fix", Linus routes the PR to a human instead of rejecting it: generated oracles 91 can be wrong, and that disagreement is exactly when a person should look. 92 93 ## Results 94 95 Every row is a real run of `uv run linus eval` against the demo month (11 PRs 96 through v4). Ground truth 97 lives in `expected.json`, which the agent never sees. Full history: 98 [`evals/SCORECARD.md`](evals/SCORECARD.md). 99 100 | Version | What changed | Accuracy | False-pay | Missed-good | 101 |---|---|---:|---:|---:| 102 | v1 | First full run; crashed while settling, resumed from checkpoints | 100% | 0% | 0% | 103 | v2 | Recalibrated points; oracles generated fresh | 91% | 0% | 20% | 104 | v3 | JEV audits every generated test case | 91% | 0% | 20% | 105 | v4 | Cases rendered from JSON; oracles must fail for a real reason | 100% (5 cold runs) | 0% | 0% | 106 107 - **v1** got every verdict right, then crashed while settling (a JSON round-trip 108 bug). All 11 verdicts were checkpointed, so the resumed run finished with zero 109 repeated API calls. 110 - **v2** ran with freshly generated oracles and **rejected a correct PR**: the 111 model wrote `slugify("Café & Tea / Coffee") == "caf--tea-coffee"`, a double 112 dash that contradicts the issue's own rule. 113 - **v3** made JEV audit every generated case before it is used. Replaying v2's 114 bad case through the audit drops it (p=0.07) and keeps the correct version 115 (p=0.87); that replay is a live regression test in `tests/test_live_audit.py`. 116 v3 also exposed a second bug: expected values rendered as code 117 (`== hello-world`), so the oracle "reproduced" the bug by crashing with 118 `NameError`. 119 - **v4** renders expected values from JSON and only trusts an oracle that fails 120 on the base code for a real reason. 100% on 5 cold runs in a row. (In those 121 runs the generator didn't produce a contradicting case, so the audit had 122 nothing to drop; it is there for the runs where it does.) 123 124 Honest caveat: 13 PRs I wrote myself is a small, friendly eval set. It shows 125 the mechanisms work; it doesn't prove they generalize. Harder cases are next. 126 127 ## Cost 128 129 Measured on v4 cold runs (11 PRs), where every oracle is generated from scratch: 130 131 | | Tokens per month (11 PRs) | Cost | 132 |---|---:|---:| 133 | JEV (all decisions and audits) | ~16k | $0.0007 | 134 | OpenAI `gpt-5.4-mini` (oracles only) | ~6k | $0.010 | 135 | **Model cost per PR** | | **$0.0010** | 136 137 Agent time: about 25 seconds for the whole month. Re-running a month reuses the 138 oracles (one per issue), so it costs only the JEV calls. 139 140 ## Quickstart 141 142 Needs Python 3.10+, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), Docker, and API keys for 143 JEV and OpenAI (neatlogs is optional for running, required for traces). 144 145 ```bash 146 cp .env.example .env # add JEV_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, NEATLOGS_API_KEY 147 make judge # build sandbox, run tests, run the close, score it 148 ``` 149 150 Every command runs through `uv run` (or activate `.venv` first): 151 152 | Command | What it does | 153 |---|---| 154 | `uv run linus doctor` | Checks keys, JEV, OpenAI, Docker, the sandbox image, Entire | 155 | `uv run linus demo` | Builds the demo month (library, issues, 13 PR branches) | 156 | `uv run linus close` | Runs the month-end close and proposes a ledger | 157 | `uv run linus close --resume latest` | Resumes a crashed run from its per-PR checkpoints | 158 | `uv run linus eval` | Fresh cold run, scored against ground truth, appended to the scorecard | 159 | `uv run linus receipt ` | Re-runs a receipt's sandbox proof, no LLM calls, and compares | 160 | `uv run linus approve ` | Appends a proposed run to the hash-chained ledger | 161 | `uv run linus ledger` | Verifies every hash in the ledger | 162 163 Rules for the pool live in [`bounty.yml`](bounty.yml): budget per currency, 164 point table, cap, minimum payout, duplicate threshold, excluded authors. 165 166 ## Evidence for the hackathon tools 167 168 - **neatlogs.** Every close is one trace: a `month_end_close` workflow span, an 169 agent span per PR, JEV calls as LLM spans with tokens and cost, OpenAI calls 170 auto-captured, every Docker run as a tool span, plus anti-gaming and 171 invariant guardrail spans. Runs since the v4 cost-tracking change print 172 their trace id, and new scorecard rows record it. Earlier runs, including 173 v2, didn't print it. 174 - **Entire.** Enabled for Claude Code in this repo (hooks in 175 `.claude/settings.json`) with PII redaction on. Checkpoints are recorded 176 for coding sessions run inside the repo, from October 12; see them with 177 `entire checkpoint list`. 178 - **cfo.ai.** Business plan in progress, built from the measured cost per PR 179 above (inputs in [`hackathon.md`](hackathon.md)). 180 - **JEV (TypeSafe).** The decision engine for every cheap judgement, following 181 its guidance: one state, many atomic questions, arithmetic in code, 182 confidence-gated routing. 183 184 ## Limitations 185 186 - The demo month is small and self-made; real repositories are messier. 187 - The sandbox runs Python projects with pytest. Other ecosystems need their own 188 runners. 189 - PRs are read from a local git repo plus a fixture file. A read-only GitHub 190 source is next. 191 - Linus proposes payouts; it doesn't move money. 192 193 Built during [neatHack](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon), October 2026. 194

1	"""Where PRs come from. LocalSource reads a bounty month stored on disk: a git
2	repo with one branch per PR, plus fixture.json with what GitHub would report
3	(issues, PR titles, bodies, authors, dates). See demo.py for the format.
4	"""

7	import re
8	import subprocess
9	import tarfile
10	import io
11	from dataclasses import dataclass
12	from pathlib import Path
13	
14	LINKED_ISSUE = re.compile(r"(?i)\b(?:fix(?:e[sd])?|close[sd]?|resolve[sd]?)\s*:?\s+#(\d+)")
15	
16	
17	@dataclass(frozen=True)
18	class Issue:
19	    number: int
20	    title: str
21	    body: str
22	    labels: tuple[str, ...] = ()
23	
24	
25	@dataclass(frozen=True)
26	class PullRequest:
27	    number: int
28	    title: str
29	    body: str
30	    author: str
31	    created_at: str
32	    base_sha: str
33	    head_sha: str
34	    issue_numbers: tuple[int, ...]
35	
36	
37	@dataclass(frozen=True)
38	class FileChange:
39	    path: str
40	    status: str  # A, M, D or R
41	    added: int
42	    removed: int
43	
44	
45	def linked_issues(text: str) -> tuple[int, ...]:
46	    return tuple(dict.fromkeys(int(n) for n in LINKED_ISSUE.findall(text)))
47	
48	
49	class LocalSource:
50	    def __init__(self, root: Path) -> None:
51	        self.root = root
52	        self.repo = root / "repo"
53	        fixture = json.loads((root / "fixture.json").read_text())
54	        self.name = fixture["repo"]
55	        self.period = fixture["period"]
56	        self.issues = {
57	            i["number"]: Issue(i["number"], i["title"], i["body"], tuple(i.get("labels", ())))
58	            for i in fixture["issues"]
59	        }
60	        self._pulls = fixture["pulls"]
61	
62	    def _git(self, *args: str) -> str:
63	        out = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=self.repo, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
64	        return out.stdout
65	
66	    def pulls(self) -> list[PullRequest]:
67	        result = []
68	        for p in sorted(self._pulls, key=lambda p: (p["created_at"], p["number"])):
69	            head = self._git("rev-parse", p["branch"]).strip()
70	            base = self._git("merge-base", p["base"], p["branch"]).strip()
71	            result.append(PullRequest(
72	                number=p["number"], title=p["title"], body=p["body"], author=p["author"],
73	                created_at=p["created_at"], base_sha=base, head_sha=head,
74	                issue_numbers=linked_issues(f"{p['title']}\n{p['body']}"),
75	            ))
76	        return result
77	
78	    def diff(self, pr: PullRequest) -> str:
79	        return self._git("diff", "--no-color", "--no-renames", "--unified=3", pr.base_sha, pr.head_sha)
80	
81	    def changes(self, pr: PullRequest) -> list[FileChange]:
82	        """Renames show as a delete plus an add, so both paths are attributed."""
83	        statuses = {}
84	        for line in self._git("diff", "--no-renames", "--name-status", pr.base_sha, pr.head_sha).splitlines():
85	            parts = line.split("\t")
86	            statuses[parts[-1]] = parts[0][0]
87	        changes = []
88	        for line in self._git("diff", "--no-renames", "--numstat", pr.base_sha, pr.head_sha).splitlines():
89	            added, removed, path = line.split("\t", 2)
90	            changes.append(FileChange(path, statuses.get(path, "M"),
91	                                      int(added) if added != "-" else 0,
92	                                      int(removed) if removed != "-" else 0))
93	        return changes
94	
95	    def files_at(self, sha: str) -> list[str]:
96	        return self._git("ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", sha).splitlines()
97	
98	    def read(self, sha: str, path: str) -> str | None:
99	        try:
100	            return self._git("show", f"{sha}:{path}")
101	        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
102	            return None
103	
104	    def export(self, sha: str, dest: Path) -> None:
105	        """Write the tree at `sha` into `dest` (no .git directory)."""
106	        archive = subprocess.run(["git", "archive", "--format=tar", sha], cwd=self.repo,
107	                                 capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
108	        dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
109	        with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(archive)) as tar:
110	            tar.extractall(dest, filter="data")

39	def conflicting(answers: dict, signals: DiffSignals, oracle_run: dict) -> bool:
40	    """The sandbox says 'not fixed' but everything else says 'honest, complete fix'.
41	
42	    Oracles are generated, so they can be wrong. When a minority of cases fail and
43	    JEV is confident the diff fully fixes the issue with no gaming signals, don't
44	    auto-reject: route it to a human. (Never auto-pays either.)
45	    """
46	    addresses = answers.get("addresses_issue", {}).get("probabilities", {})
47	    full_fix = float(addresses.get("2", addresses.get(2, 0))) >= 0.8
48	    honest = (answers.get("special_casing", {}).get("noul", 1) < 0.5
49	              and answers.get("claims_match", {}).get("noul", 0) >= 0.5
50	              and not signals.tampering)
51	    total = oracle_run["passed"] + oracle_run["failed"]
52	    minority = total > 0 and oracle_run["failed"] * 3 <= total
53	    return full_fix and honest and minority

84	    def __init__(self, settings: Settings, source: LocalSource, policy: Policy, ui,
85	                 run_id: str | None = None, crash_after: int | None = None,
86	                 reuse_oracles: bool = True) -> None:
87	        self.settings, self.source, self.policy, self.ui = settings, source, policy, ui
88	        self.reuse_oracles = reuse_oracles
89	        self.store = Store(settings.state_dir / "linus.db")
90	        self.jev = Jev(settings)
91	        self.gen = Generator(settings)
92	        self.crash_after = crash_after
93	        self.resumed = run_id is not None
94	        # The random suffix keeps two runs started in the same second apart.
95	        self.run_id = run_id or (f"{source.period}-{datetime.now(timezone.utc):%Y%m%d-%H%M%S}"
96	                                 f"-{secrets.token_hex(2)}")
97	        self.run_dir = settings.state_dir / "runs" / self.run_id
98	        self.workdir = settings.state_dir / "work"
99	        self.workdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

101	    # -- per PR ---------------------------------------------------------------
102	
103	    def _issue(self, pr: PullRequest) -> Issue | None:
104	        for n in pr.issue_numbers:
105	            issue = self.source.issues.get(n)
106	            if issue and set(issue.labels) & set(self.policy.issue_labels):
107	                return issue
108	        return None
109	
110	    def _gate(self, pr: PullRequest, issue: Issue | None, data: dict) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
111	        diff = self.source.diff(pr)
112	        signals = diffcheck.analyze(diff, self.source.changes(pr), f"{pr.title}\n{pr.body}")
113	        data["signals"] = asdict(signals)
114	        data["issue"] = issue.number if issue else None
115	        if why := self.policy.excluded(pr.author):
116	            return "reject", why
117	        if signals.manipulates_outcome:
118	            return "reject", "changes test outcomes instead of the code: " + "; ".join(signals.outcome_hacks[:3])
119	        if signals.docs_only and not self.policy.include_docs:
120	            return "reject", "docs-only PRs are not eligible under bounty.yml"
121	        if not signals.docs_only and issue is None:
122	            return "reject", "does not fix an issue labelled for this bounty"
123	        gate = gates.run(self.jev, pr, issue, diff, signals)
124	        data["gate"] = asdict(gate)
125	        if gate.decision == "reject":
126	            return "reject", gate.reason
127	        return None, ""

129	    def _oracle(self, issue: Issue, pr: PullRequest, signals: DiffSignals) -> Oracle:
130	        # Only a valid oracle in the current format is reused: a failed build may have
131	        # been bad luck or a Docker problem. Infrastructure errors propagate before
132	        # anything is cached.

251	                    f"identical), submitted later", closest.number, sims[closest.number])

"""SQLite state. Every PR's progress is saved the moment a stage finishes, so a
crashed run resumes where it stopped instead of re-verifying (or re-paying).
"""

import json
import sqlite3
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS runs (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, created_at TEXT, repo TEXT, period TEXT,
    status TEXT, summary TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS items (
    run_id TEXT, pr INTEGER, stage TEXT, verdict TEXT, data TEXT, updated_at TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (run_id, pr)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oracles (
    repo TEXT, issue INTEGER, base_sha TEXT, data TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (repo, issue, base_sha)
);
"""


def now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")


class Store:
    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.db = sqlite3.connect(path)
        self.db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self.db.executescript(SCHEMA)

    def create_run(self, run_id: str, repo: str, period: str) -> None:
        with self.db:
            self.db.execute("INSERT INTO runs VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'running', '{}')",
                            (run_id, now(), repo, period))

    def run(self, run_id: str) -> dict | None:
        row = self.db.execute("SELECT * FROM runs WHERE id = ?", (run_id,)).fetchone()
        return dict(row) if row else None

    def runs(self) -> list[dict]:
        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute("SELECT * FROM runs ORDER BY created_at DESC")]

    def latest_unfinished(self, repo: str, period: str) -> str | None:
        row = self.db.execute(
            "SELECT id FROM runs WHERE repo = ? AND period = ? AND status = 'running' "
            "ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1", (repo, period)).fetchone()
        return row["id"] if row else None

    def finish_run(self, run_id: str, status: str, summary: dict) -> None:
        with self.db:
            self.db.execute("UPDATE runs SET status = ?, summary = ? WHERE id = ?",
                            (status, json.dumps(summary, default=str), run_id))

    def item(self, run_id: str, pr: int) -> dict | None:
        row = self.db.execute("SELECT * FROM items WHERE run_id = ? AND pr = ?", (run_id, pr)).fetchone()
        if not row:
            return None
        return {"stage": row["stage"], "verdict": row["verdict"], "data": json.loads(row["data"])}

    def items(self, run_id: str) -> dict[int, dict]:
        rows = self.db.execute("SELECT * FROM items WHERE run_id = ?", (run_id,))
        return {r["pr"]: {"stage": r["stage"], "verdict": r["verdict"], "data": json.loads(r["data"])}
                for r in rows}

    def save_item(self, run_id: str, pr: int, stage: str, verdict: str | None, data: dict) -> None:
        with self.db:
            self.db.execute(
                "INSERT INTO items VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT (run_id, pr) DO UPDATE SET "
                "stage = excluded.stage, verdict = excluded.verdict, data = excluded.data, "
                "updated_at = excluded.updated_at",
                (run_id, pr, stage, verdict, json.dumps(data, default=str), now()))

    def oracle(self, repo: str, issue: int, base_sha: str) -> dict | None:
        row = self.db.execute("SELECT data FROM oracles WHERE repo = ? AND issue = ? AND base_sha = ?",
                              (repo, issue, base_sha)).fetchone()
        return json.loads(row["data"]) if row else None

    def save_oracle(self, repo: str, issue: int, base_sha: str, data: dict) -> None:
        with self.db:
            self.db.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO oracles VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                            (repo, issue, base_sha, json.dumps(data, default=str)))

def score(summary: dict, expected: dict) -> dict:
    rows = []
    for n, exp in sorted(expected.items(), key=lambda kv: int(kv[0])):
        verdicts = summary["verdicts"]
        got = verdicts.get(int(n)) or verdicts.get(str(n))
        rows.append({"pr": int(n), "author": got["author"], "expected": exp["verdict"],
                     "got": got["verdict"], "ok": got["verdict"] == exp["verdict"],
                     "why_expected": exp["why"], "reason": got["reason"]})
    good = [r for r in rows if r["expected"] == "pay"]
    bad = [r for r in rows if r["expected"] == "reject"]
    false_pay = [r["pr"] for r in bad if r["got"] == "pay"]
    missed = [r["pr"] for r in good if r["got"] == "reject"]
    flagged = [r["pr"] for r in rows if r["got"] == "flag"]
    cost = summary["cost"]
    return {
        "run_id": summary["run_id"],
        "trace_id": summary.get("trace_id") or "",
        "accuracy": sum(r["ok"] for r in rows) / len(rows),
        "false_pay_rate": len(false_pay) / len(bad) if bad else 0.0,
        "missed_good_rate": len(missed) / len(good) if good else 0.0,
        "human_flag_rate": len(flagged) / len(rows),
        "false_pay": false_pay, "missed_good": missed, "flagged": flagged,
        "jev_usd": cost["jev_usd"], "openai_tokens": cost["openai_tokens"],
        "openai_usd": cost.get("openai_usd"), "usd_per_pr": cost.get("usd_per_pr"),
        "seconds_per_pr": cost["pr_seconds"] / max(cost["prs"], 1),
        "rows": rows,
    }

"""Receipts and the tamper-evident ledger.

A receipt is canonical JSON of everything behind one PR's verdict; its
SHA-256 goes into the ledger. The ledger is append-only JSONL where each
entry carries the hash of the one before it, so editing any past entry breaks
every hash after it.
"""

import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

GENESIS = "0" * 64


def canonical(data: dict) -> bytes:
    return json.dumps(data, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), default=str).encode()


def sha256(data: dict) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical(data)).hexdigest()


def write_receipt(directory: Path, number: int, receipt: dict) -> tuple[Path, str]:
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = directory / f"pr-{number}.json"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2, sort_keys=True, default=str))
    return path, sha256(receipt)


def read(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    if not path.exists():
        return []
    return [json.loads(line) for line in path.read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]


def append(path: Path, entries: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    existing = read(path)
    prev = existing[-1]["hash"] if existing else GENESIS
    seq = existing[-1]["seq"] + 1 if existing else 1
    written = []
    with path.open("a") as f:
        for entry in entries:
            body = {**entry, "seq": seq, "prev": prev}
            body["hash"] = sha256(body)
            f.write(json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
            written.append(body)
            prev, seq = body["hash"], seq + 1
    return written


def verify_chain(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    problems = []
    prev = GENESIS
    for i, entry in enumerate(read(path), start=1):
        body = {k: v for k, v in entry.items() if k != "hash"}
        if entry.get("prev") != prev:
            problems.append(f"entry {i}: prev hash does not match entry {i - 1}")
        if sha256(body) != entry.get("hash"):
            problems.append(f"entry {i}: contents were modified (hash mismatch)")
        prev = entry.get("hash", "")
    return problems


def _cents(amount) -> int:
    return round(float(amount) * 100)


def _payout_problems(entry: dict, receipts_dir: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Each paid PR must have an unchanged receipt that says pay, for this author."""
    who, prs, hashes = entry.get("contributor"), entry.get("prs") or [], entry.get("receipts") or []
    if not prs or len(prs) != len(hashes):
        return [f"{who}: payout lists {len(prs)} PRs but {len(hashes)} receipts"]
    problems = []
    for number, digest in zip(prs, hashes):
        path = receipts_dir / f"pr-{number}.json"
        if not path.exists():
            problems.append(f"#{number}: no receipt in this run")
            continue
        receipt = json.loads(path.read_text())
        if sha256(receipt) != digest:
            problems.append(f"#{number}: receipt does not match the hash in the proposal")
        if (receipt.get("pr") or {}).get("author") != who:
            problems.append(f"#{number}: paid to {who} but authored by {(receipt.get('pr') or {}).get('author')}")
        if receipt.get("verdict") != "pay":
            problems.append(f"#{number}: receipt verdict is {receipt.get('verdict')}, not pay")
    return problems


def proposal_problems(raw: bytes, summary: dict, receipts_dir: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Why a proposed ledger must not be appended, if anything. It must be the
    exact file the close wrote, and its entries must still hold the invariants."""
    expected = summary.get("proposal_sha256")
    if not expected:
        return ["the run has no recorded proposal hash; re-run the close"]
    if hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() != expected:
        return ["ledger.proposed.jsonl changed since the close wrote it"]
    budgets = {a["currency"]: _cents(a["budget"]) for a in summary.get("allocations", [])}
    totals = dict.fromkeys(budgets, 0)
    problems = []
    for entry in (json.loads(line) for line in raw.decode().splitlines() if line.strip()):
        if (entry.get("run_id"), entry.get("repo")) != (summary.get("run_id"), summary.get("repo")):
            problems.append(f"entry for run {entry.get('run_id')} / {entry.get('repo')} is not from this run")
        currency = entry.get("currency")
        if currency not in totals:
            problems.append(f"entry in {currency}, which is not in this run's budget")
            continue
        totals[currency] += _cents(entry.get("amount", 0))
        if entry.get("type") == "payout":
            problems += _payout_problems(entry, receipts_dir)
        elif entry.get("type") != "rollover":
            problems.append(f"unexpected entry type {entry.get('type')!r}")
    for currency, cents in budgets.items():
        if totals[currency] != cents:
            problems.append(f"{currency}: payouts + rollover = {totals[currency] / 100:.2f}, "
                            f"budget is {cents / 100:.2f}")
    return problems


def paid_prs(path: Path, repo: str) -> set[int]:
    return {n for e in read(path) if e.get("type") == "payout" and e.get("repo") == repo
            for n in e.get("prs", [])}

@dataclass
class Verification:
    outcome: str  # verified | not_fixed | regression | tampering | needs_human | inconclusive
    reason: str
    runs: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)


def _copy_base_tests(source: LocalSource, base_sha: str, tree: Path) -> int:
    count = 0
    for path in source.files_at(base_sha):
        if TEST_PATH.search(path) and path.endswith(".py"):
            target = tree / BASE_TESTS_DIR / path
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_text(source.read(base_sha, path) or "")
            count += 1
    return count


def verify(source: LocalSource, pr: PullRequest, oracle: Oracle | None,
           signals: DiffSignals, workdir: Path) -> Verification:
    tree = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=f"pr{pr.number}-", dir=workdir))
    runs: list[dict] = []
    try:
        source.export(pr.head_sha, tree)

        if oracle is not None:
            repro = run_oracle(tree, oracle.test_code, label=f"pr{pr.number}_oracle")
            runs.append(repro.to_dict())
            if repro.outcome == "error":
                why = repro.problem or "oracle test did not run cleanly on the PR code"
                return Verification("inconclusive", why, runs)
            if repro.outcome == "fail":
                total = repro.passed + repro.failed
                return Verification(
                    "not_fixed", f"reproduction test still fails on the PR ({repro.failed} of {total} failing)",
                    runs)
            if repro.passed != oracle.case_count:
                return Verification(
                    "inconclusive", f"oracle has {oracle.case_count} cases but {repro.passed} passed", runs)

        copied = _copy_base_tests(source, pr.base_sha, tree)
        targets = [d for d in ("tests", "test") if (tree / d).is_dir()]
        if copied:
            targets.append(BASE_TESTS_DIR)
        suite = pytest(tree, targets or ["."], label=f"pr{pr.number}_suite")
        runs.append(suite.to_dict())

        if suite.outcome == "pass":
            proof = "fails on base, passes on PR" if oracle else "docs only"
            return Verification("verified", f"{proof}; full suite incl. base tests green ({suite.passed} passed)", runs)
        if suite.outcome == "error":
            why = suite.problem or "test suite did not run cleanly on the PR code"
            return Verification("inconclusive", why, runs)
        if signals.tampering:
            removed = ", ".join(signals.removed_tests) or f"{signals.added_skips} skip marker(s)"
            return Verification(
                "tampering", f"deletes or skips tests ({removed}) that its change breaks", runs)
        if signals.touches_tests:
            return Verification("needs_human", "existing tests fail and the PR also edits tests", runs)
        return Verification("regression", f"breaks existing tests ({suite.failed} failing)", runs)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tree, ignore_errors=True)

def compact(response) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Answers as plain JSON: nouls as probabilities, scores with level and confidence."""
    out: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for name, answer in response.answers.items():
        if answer.type == "noul":
            out[name] = {"noul": round(answer.noul, 3)}
        elif answer.type == "score":
            probs = {int(k): round(v, 3) for k, v in answer.probabilities.items()}
            out[name] = {"score": round(answer.score, 3), "confidence": round(answer.confidence, 3),
                         "probabilities": probs, "legend": {int(k): v for k, v in answer.legend.items()}}
        else:
            out[name] = {"choice": answer.choice, "confidence": round(answer.confidence, 3),
                         "probabilities": answer.probabilities}
    return out


def top_level(answer: dict) -> int:
    probs = {int(k): v for k, v in answer["probabilities"].items()}
    return max(probs, key=lambda k: probs[k])

# jev-1.13 pricing: $0.042 per million input tokens; output tokens are free.
USD_PER_INPUT_TOKEN = 0.042 / 1_000_000


def _dump(value: Any, limit: int = 20_000) -> str:
    return json.dumps(value, default=str)[:limit]


class Jev:
    def __init__(self, settings: Settings) -> None:
        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
            "api_key": settings.jev_api_key,
            "model": settings.jev_model,
            "timeout": 30.0,
        }
        if settings.jev_base_url:
            kwargs["base_url"] = settings.jev_base_url
        self._client = TypeSafeClient(**kwargs)
        self.calls = 0
        self.input_tokens = 0

    @property
    def cost_usd(self) -> float:
        return self.input_tokens * USD_PER_INPUT_TOKEN

    def ask(self, step: str, state: Any, questions: Mapping[str, Question]) -> SystemOneResponse:
        """One System One request, traced in neatlogs as an LLM span."""
        with trace(name=f"jev.{step}", kind="LLM") as span:
            span.set_attribute("neatlogs.internal", False)
            span.set_attribute("neatlogs.llm.provider", "typesafe")
            span.set_attribute("neatlogs.llm.system", "jev")
            span.set_attribute(
                "input.value",
                _dump({"state": state, "questions": {k: q.model_dump() for k, q in questions.items()}}),
            )
            response = self._client.system_one(state=state, questions=questions)
            tokens = response.usage.input_tokens
            self.calls += 1
            self.input_tokens += tokens
            span.set_attribute("neatlogs.llm.model_name", response.model)
            span.set_attribute("neatlogs.llm.token_count.prompt", tokens)
            span.set_attribute("neatlogs.llm.token_count.completion", response.usage.output_tokens)
            span.set_attribute("neatlogs.llm.token_count.total", tokens + response.usage.output_tokens)
            span.set_attribute("linus.cost_usd", tokens * USD_PER_INPUT_TOKEN)
            span.set_attribute("output.value", _dump(response.model_dump()["answers"]))
        return response

"""`linus demo --publish OWNER/REPO`: puts the demo month on GitHub as a real
public repo, so anyone can watch Linus judge real PRs, or open one and try to
fool it.

Idempotent: the repo, labels, issues (matched by title) and PRs (matched by
head branch) that already exist are left alone. Branches are pushed with git
and the machine's own git credentials; everything else goes through the API.
"""

import json
import os
import subprocess
from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path

from linus import demo
from linus.github import BOUNTY_LABEL, VERDICT_LABELS, GitHub, GitHubError, split_repo
from linus.source import LINKED_ISSUE

DESCRIPTION = "Live demo for Linus: a bounty month with real PRs. Open a PR, or try to fool the bot."


class PublishError(Exception):
    pass


def _git(repo_dir: Path, *args: str) -> str:
    out = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=repo_dir, capture_output=True, text=True,
                         env=dict(os.environ, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT="0"))
    if out.returncode != 0:
        raise PublishError(f"git {args[0]} failed: {(out.stderr or out.stdout).strip()[:300]}")
    return out.stdout.strip()


def _ensure_repo(gh: GitHub, repo: str, log: Callable[[str], None]) -> None:
    owner, name = split_repo(repo)
    if gh.exists(f"/repos/{repo}"):
        log(f"repo {repo} exists")
        return
    if gh.login().lower() != owner.lower():
        raise PublishError(f"{repo} doesn't exist and can only be created under your own account "
                           f"({gh.login()})")
    gh.post("/user/repos", {"name": name, "description": DESCRIPTION, "private": False, "auto_init": False,
                            "has_issues": True})
    log(f"created public repo {repo}")


def _push(repo_dir: Path, remote: str, repo: str, branches: list[str], force: bool,
          log: Callable[[str], None]) -> None:
    main = demo.readme_commit(repo_dir, repo)
    listed = _git(repo_dir, "ls-remote", remote, "refs/heads/main")
    remote_main = listed.split()[0] if listed else None
    if remote_main and remote_main != main and not force:
        raise PublishError(f"{repo} already has a main branch that differs from the demo's "
                           f"({remote_main[:12]} vs {main[:12]}); pass --force to overwrite it")
    flags = ["--force"] if force or remote_main is None else []
    # main goes first and alone, so an empty repo takes it as its default branch.
    _git(repo_dir, "push", "--quiet", *flags, remote, f"{main}:refs/heads/main")
    _git(repo_dir, "push", "--quiet", *flags, remote, *[f"refs/heads/{b}:refs/heads/{b}" for b in branches])
    log(f"pushed main ({main[:12]}, demo README) and {len(branches)} PR branches"
        + (" (forced)" if flags else ""))


def _issues(gh: GitHub, repo: str, issues: list[dict], log: Callable[[str], None]) -> dict[int, int]:
    """Create the bounty issues in order. Returns demo issue number -> GitHub number."""
    existing = {i["title"]: i["number"] for i in gh.paginate(f"/repos/{repo}/issues", state="all")
                if "pull_request" not in i}
    numbers = {}
    for issue in sorted(issues, key=lambda i: i["number"]):
        if issue["title"] not in existing:
            created = gh.post(f"/repos/{repo}/issues", {"title": issue["title"], "body": issue["body"],
                                                        "labels": issue["labels"]})
            existing[issue["title"]] = created["number"]
            log(f"created issue #{created['number']} {issue['title']}")
        numbers[issue["number"]] = existing[issue["title"]]
    if moved := {d: g for d, g in numbers.items() if d != g}:
        log(f"issues got different numbers than in the demo ({moved}); PR links are rewritten to match")
    return numbers


def relink(body: str, numbers: dict[int, int]) -> str:
    """Point "Fixes #N" at the issue's number on GitHub."""
    def swap(m):
        n = int(m.group(1))
        return m.group(0)[: m.start(1) - m.start(0)] + str(numbers.get(n, n))

    return LINKED_ISSUE.sub(swap, body)


def _pulls(gh: GitHub, repo: str, pulls: list[dict], numbers: dict[int, int], log: Callable[[str], None]) -> None:
    existing = {p["head"]["ref"] for p in gh.paginate(f"/repos/{repo}/pulls", state="all")}
    for pr in sorted(pulls, key=lambda p: (p["created_at"], p["number"])):
        if pr["branch"] in existing:
            continue
        body = f"{relink(pr['body'], numbers)}\n\nDemo contributor: {pr['author']}"
        created = gh.post(f"/repos/{repo}/pulls", {"title": pr["title"], "head": pr["branch"],
                                                   "base": pr["base"], "body": body})
        log(f"opened PR #{created['number']} {pr['title']} ({pr['author']})")


def publish(root: Path, repo: str, gh: GitHub, force: bool = False, remote: str | None = None,
            log: Callable[[str], None] = print) -> None:
    """Publish the demo month built under `root` (see demo.build) as `repo`."""
    split_repo(repo)
    fixture = json.loads((root / "fixture.json").read_text())
    remote = remote or f"https://github.com/{repo}.git"
    _ensure_repo(gh, repo, log)
    _push(root / "repo", remote, repo, [p["branch"] for p in fixture["pulls"]], force, log)
    try:
        if gh.get(f"/repos/{repo}").get("default_branch") != "main":
            gh.patch(f"/repos/{repo}", {"default_branch": "main"})
    except GitHubError as exc:
        log(f"could not set the default branch to main: {exc}")
    if created := gh.ensure_labels(repo, [BOUNTY_LABEL, *VERDICT_LABELS.values()]):
        log(f"created labels: {', '.join(created)}")
    numbers = _issues(gh, repo, fixture["issues"], log)
    _pulls(gh, repo, fixture["pulls"], numbers, log)

"""`linus economics`: unit costs for the business plan, from real runs.

Measured values come from eval results (evals/results/*.json) and the run
summaries and per-PR items in the store. The headline is taken from cold runs,
where every oracle is generated from scratch, so it is the expensive case.
Projections multiply those measurements by assumptions that are passed in
explicitly and labelled as such in every output.
"""

import csv
import json
from pathlib import Path

from linus.jev import USD_PER_INPUT_TOKEN
from linus.llm import usd
from linus.store import Store

VOLUMES = (100, 1_000, 10_000)


def pr_cost_usd(cost: dict, openai_model: str) -> tuple[float, float | None]:
    """(JEV, OpenAI) dollars for one PR's recorded token counts; OpenAI is None
    when the model's price is unknown."""
    jev = cost.get("jev_tokens", 0) * USD_PER_INPUT_TOKEN
    return jev, usd(openai_model, cost.get("openai_in", 0), cost.get("openai_out", 0))


def sandbox_runs(items: dict) -> int:
    """Docker runs behind a run: every verification run, plus the base-code runs
    that built each distinct oracle (counted once per oracle, as on a cold run)."""
    count, oracles = 0, {}
    for item in items.values():
        data = item["data"]
        count += len((data.get("verification") or {}).get("runs") or [])
        if oracle := data.get("oracle"):
            oracles[(oracle.get("issue"), oracle.get("test_sha256"))] = oracle
    return count + sum(1 for o in oracles.values() for a in o.get("attempts") or [] if a.get("base_outcome"))


def collect(evals_dir: Path, store: Store | None) -> list[dict]:
    """One row per run, merging an eval result with the stored summary of the same run."""
    runs: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for path in sorted(evals_dir.glob("results/*.json")):
        r = json.loads(path.read_text())
        prs = len(r.get("rows") or [])
        runs[r["run_id"]] = {
            "run_id": r["run_id"], "label": r.get("label", ""), "from": "eval", "repo": "",
            "cold": r.get("cold", True),  # `linus eval` always ran cold until --run existed
            "prs": prs, "jev_usd": r.get("jev_usd"), "openai_usd": r.get("openai_usd"),
            "agent_seconds": r["seconds_per_pr"] * prs if "seconds_per_pr" in r else None,
            "sandbox_runs": None,
        }
    for row in store.runs() if store else []:
        summary = json.loads(row["summary"] or "{}")
        cost = summary.get("cost")
        if row["status"] == "running" or not cost or not cost.get("prs"):
            continue
        run = runs.setdefault(row["id"], {"run_id": row["id"], "label": "", "from": "store",
                                          "cold": summary.get("cold")})
        if run["from"] == "eval":
            run["from"] = "eval+store"
        run |= {"repo": summary.get("repo", ""), "prs": cost["prs"], "jev_usd": cost.get("jev_usd"),
                "openai_usd": cost.get("openai_usd"), "agent_seconds": cost.get("pr_seconds"),
                "sandbox_runs": sandbox_runs(store.items(row["id"]))}
    rows = sorted(runs.values(), key=lambda r: r["run_id"])
    for r in rows:
        prs = max(r["prs"], 1)
        r["jev_usd_per_pr"] = r["jev_usd"] / prs if r["jev_usd"] is not None else None
        r["openai_usd_per_pr"] = r["openai_usd"] / prs if r["openai_usd"] is not None else None
        r["agent_seconds_per_pr"] = r["agent_seconds"] / prs if r["agent_seconds"] is not None else None
        r["sandbox_runs_per_pr"] = r["sandbox_runs"] / prs if r["sandbox_runs"] is not None else None
    return rows


def _pooled(rows: list[dict], key: str) -> float | None:
    """Total of `key` over total PRs, for the runs that recorded it."""
    have = [r for r in rows if r.get(key) is not None and r["prs"]]
    return sum(r[key] for r in have) / sum(r["prs"] for r in have) if have else None


def measure(rows: list[dict]) -> dict:
    cold = [r for r in rows if r["cold"] and r["jev_usd"] is not None and r["openai_usd"] is not None]
    basis = cold or [r for r in rows if r["jev_usd"] is not None and r["openai_usd"] is not None]
    jev, openai = _pooled(basis, "jev_usd"), _pooled(basis, "openai_usd")
    return {
        "basis": "cold runs" if cold else "all runs (no cold run recorded both costs)",
        "cold_runs_used": len(cold),
        "runs_used": len(basis),
        "prs_measured": sum(r["prs"] for r in basis),
        "jev_usd_per_run": sum(r["jev_usd"] for r in basis) / len(basis) if basis else None,
        "openai_usd_per_run": sum(r["openai_usd"] for r in basis) / len(basis) if basis else None,
        "jev_usd_per_pr": jev,
        "openai_usd_per_pr": openai,
        "model_usd_per_pr": jev + openai if basis else None,
        "agent_seconds_per_pr": _pooled(basis, "agent_seconds"),
        "sandbox_runs_per_pr": _pooled(rows, "sandbox_runs"),
    }


def project(measured: dict, price_per_repo: float, sandbox_usd_per_pr: float, real_repo_multiplier: float,
            volumes=VOLUMES) -> list[dict]:
    """One repo with `volume` PRs a month, priced at `price_per_repo` a month."""
    rows = []
    model_per_pr = (measured["model_usd_per_pr"] or 0) * real_repo_multiplier
    for volume in volumes:
        model, sandbox = model_per_pr * volume, sandbox_usd_per_pr * volume
        cost = model + sandbox
        rows.append({
            "prs_per_month": volume, "model_usd": round(model, 4), "sandbox_usd": round(sandbox, 4),
            "cost_usd": round(cost, 4), "cost_per_pr_usd": round(cost / volume, 6),
            "price_usd": price_per_repo, "gross_margin": round((price_per_repo - cost) / price_per_repo, 4)
            if price_per_repo else None,
            "agent_hours": round((measured["agent_seconds_per_pr"] or 0) * volume / 3600, 2),
            "sandbox_runs": round((measured["sandbox_runs_per_pr"] or 0) * volume),
        })
    return rows


def build(evals_dir: Path, store: Store | None, price_per_repo: float, sandbox_usd_per_pr: float,
          real_repo_multiplier: float) -> dict:
    rows = collect(evals_dir, store)
    measured = measure(rows)
    assumptions = {"price_per_repo_usd_month": price_per_repo, "sandbox_usd_per_pr": sandbox_usd_per_pr,
                   "real_repo_multiplier": real_repo_multiplier}
    return {
        "measured": measured,
        "assumed": assumptions,
        "projection": {
            "note": "One repo with this many PRs a month. Model cost = measured model $/PR x real_repo_multiplier "
                    "(assumed); sandbox cost = sandbox_usd_per_pr (assumed); price = price_per_repo (assumed); "
                    "agent hours and sandbox runs scale the measured per-PR values.",
            "rows": project(measured, price_per_repo, sandbox_usd_per_pr, real_repo_multiplier),
        },
        "runs": rows,
    }


def write(result: dict, directory: Path) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
    """economics.json, plus economics.csv as basis,section,metric,value rows for a spreadsheet."""
    json_path, csv_path = directory / "economics.json", directory / "economics.csv"
    json_path.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    with csv_path.open("w", newline="") as f:
        out = csv.writer(f)
        out.writerow(["basis", "section", "metric", "value"])
        for key, value in result["measured"].items():
            out.writerow(["measured", "unit", key, value])
        for key, value in result["assumed"].items():
            out.writerow(["assumed", "unit", key, value])
        for row in result["projection"]["rows"]:
            for key, value in row.items():
                if key != "prs_per_month":
                    out.writerow(["projected", f"{row['prs_per_month']} PRs/month", key, value])
        for run in result["runs"]:
            for key in ("prs", "jev_usd_per_pr", "openai_usd_per_pr", "agent_seconds_per_pr", "sandbox_runs_per_pr"):
                out.writerow(["measured", f"run {run['run_id']}", key, run[key]])
    return json_path, csv_path

"""The GitHub client, offline: retries, rate limits, headers and pagination."""

import time

import httpx
import pytest

from linus.github import GitHub, GitHubError, split_repo


def _client(responses, sleeps=None):
    seen = []

    def handle(request):
        seen.append(request)
        result = responses.pop(0)
        if isinstance(result, Exception):
            raise result
        return result

    gh = GitHub("tok", transport=httpx.MockTransport(handle), sleep=(sleeps.append if sleeps is not None
                                                                    else lambda s: None))
    return gh, seen


def test_every_request_carries_the_versioned_headers():
    gh, seen = _client([httpx.Response(200, json={"login": "me"})])
    assert gh.login() == "me"
    headers = seen[0].headers
    assert headers["accept"] == "application/vnd.github+json"
    assert headers["x-github-api-version"] == "2022-11-28"
    assert headers["authorization"] == "Bearer tok"


def test_server_errors_and_network_errors_are_retried_with_backoff():
    sleeps = []
    gh, seen = _client([httpx.Response(502), httpx.ConnectError("down"), httpx.Response(200, json={"ok": 1})],
                       sleeps)
    assert gh.get("/x") == {"ok": 1}
    assert len(seen) == 3 and sleeps == [2.0, 4.0]


def test_gives_up_after_three_attempts():
    gh, seen = _client([httpx.Response(500)] * 3)
    with pytest.raises(GitHubError) as err:
        gh.get("/x")
    assert err.value.status == 500 and len(seen) == 3


def test_rate_limits_are_waited_out():
    sleeps = []
    reset = str(int(time.time()) + 5)
    gh, _ = _client([httpx.Response(429, headers={"retry-after": "7"}),
                     httpx.Response(403, headers={"x-ratelimit-remaining": "0", "x-ratelimit-reset": reset}),
                     httpx.Response(200, json=[])], sleeps)
    assert gh.get("/x") == []
    assert sleeps[0] == 7.0 and 1 <= sleeps[1] <= 7


def test_a_plain_403_is_not_retried():
    gh, seen = _client([httpx.Response(403, json={"message": "Resource not accessible"})])
    with pytest.raises(GitHubError, match="Resource not accessible"):
        gh.post("/x", {})
    assert len(seen) == 1


def test_a_rate_limit_that_resets_too_late_fails_instead_of_blocking():
    reset = str(int(time.time()) + 3600)
    gh, seen = _client([httpx.Response(403, headers={"x-ratelimit-remaining": "0", "x-ratelimit-reset": reset})])
    with pytest.raises(GitHubError):
        gh.get("/x")
    assert len(seen) == 1

# textkit: a live demo of Linus

textkit is a small Python library of text and list helpers: `chunk`,
`slugify`, `parse_duration`, `word_count` and `truncate`. It is small on
purpose. It exists to be the subject of this demo.

This repository is a live demo of [Linus](https://github.com/VARUN3WARE/Linus),
an agent that runs the month-end close for an open-source bounty pool. It
verifies every pull request with evidence it can reproduce, rejects what it
can't prove, and proposes a payout ledger that a maintainer approves.

## How the demo works

- [Issues labelled `bounty`](https://github.com/VARUN3WARE/textkit-live/issues?q=label%3Abounty) are paid from a
  monthly pool.
- The 13 pull requests are simulated contributors. All of them were opened
  by the maintainer account; the contributor names come from the commit
  authors. 5 are honest fixes. The others are attacks bounty programs
  actually see: a fix hard-coded to the issue's example, prompt injection
  aimed at AI reviewers, a "fix" that deletes the test it breaks, a copy of
  another PR, a conftest that forces a green test run, and more.
- At the close, Linus comments on every PR with its verdict and the evidence
  behind it, labels it `linus: pay`, `linus: reject` or `linus: flag`, and
  posts a "Bounty close" issue with the leaderboard.

## Try to fool the bot

Anyone may [open a pull request](https://github.com/VARUN3WARE/textkit-live/compare) against a
bounty issue (say `Fixes #N` in the description). Linus runs it in a sandbox
with no network and posts its verdict on the PR at the next close.
Wrong fixes, hard-coded answers, deleted tests, forged test runs and notes to
AI reviewers are all fair game.

No real money is paid in this demo.

## Using textkit

chunk([1, 2, 3, 4], 2)          # [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
slugify("hello")                # "hello"

import json
import re

REPO = "maintainer/textkit-live"


def _answers(addresses: int = 2) -> dict:
    return {"manipulation": {"noul": 0.02}, "claims_match": {"noul": 0.91}, "special_casing": {"noul": 0.04},
            "addresses_issue": {"score": addresses, "confidence": 0.9,
                                "probabilities": {str(i): 0.9 if i == addresses else 0.05 for i in range(3)}}}


def _receipt(number: int, author: str, verdict: str, reason: str, **extra) -> dict:
    return {"run_id": "2026-10-x", "repo": REPO, "period": "2026-10", "verdict": verdict, "reason": reason,
            "pr": {"number": number, "author": author, "title": f"PR {number}"},
            "gate": {"answers": _answers()}, "signals": {}, "verification": None, "oracle": None,
            "anti_gaming": None, "points": None, "contributor_payout": {}} | extra


PAID = _receipt(
    6, "alice-dev", "pay", "fails on base, passes on PR; full suite incl. base tests green (19 passed)",
    oracle={"issue": 1, "test_sha256": "abcdef1234567890", "cases": [{}] * 6,
            "attempts": [{"attempt": 1, "base_outcome": "fail", "base_failed": 4}]},
    verification={"runs": [{"label": "pr6_oracle", "outcome": "pass", "passed": 6, "failed": 0},
                           {"label": "pr6_suite", "outcome": "pass", "passed": 19, "failed": 0}]},
    points={"points": 30, "explanation": "(20 + 10) x 1.0"},
    contributor_payout={"USD": 600.0, "AWS credits": 300.0})
REJECTED = _receipt(
    7, "peggy-ci", "reject", "reproduction test still fails on the PR (4 of 6 failing)",
    signals={"removed_tests": ["test_truncate_short_text_unchanged"], "harness_files": ["tests/conftest.py"]},
    verification={"runs": [{"label": "pr7_oracle", "outcome": "fail", "passed": 2, "failed": 4}]})


def _summary(tmp_path, receipts=(PAID, REJECTED), status="proposed") -> dict:
    run_dir = tmp_path / "run"
    for r in receipts:
        ledger.write_receipt(run_dir / "receipts", r["pr"]["number"], r)
    return {
        "run_id": "2026-10-x", "repo": REPO, "period": "2026-10", "status": status, "source": "github",
        "problems": [] if status == "proposed" else ["USD: payouts exceed budget"], "trace_id": "f00d" * 8,
        "verdicts": {str(r["pr"]["number"]): {"author": r["pr"]["author"], "verdict": r["verdict"],
                                              "reason": r["reason"], "points": (r["points"] or {}).get("points")}
                     for r in receipts},
        "allocations": [{"currency": "USD", "budget": 2000, "payouts": {"alice-dev": 600.0}, "rollover": 1400.0},

        "run_dir": str(run_dir),

    assert github_report.report(fake_github.client(), summary, ITEMS, log=lambda m: None) == []

    [paid] = fake_github.comments(REPO, 6)
    assert paid.startswith(VERDICT_MARKER) and "**Linus verdict: PAY**" in paid
    assert "on the base code it failed (4 of 6 cases failing)" in paid
    assert "On this PR: 6 passed, 0 failed." in paid
    assert "including the base branch's tests: pass (19 passed, 0 failed)" in paid
    assert "addresses an AI reviewer p=0.02" in paid and "fixes the issue: yes (p=0.90)" in paid
    assert "Points: 30" in paid and "$600.00" in paid and "300.00 AWS credits" in paid
    assert f"Receipt sha256 `{ledger.sha256(PAID)[:12]}`" in paid

    result = {"run_id": run_id, "label": run_id, "jev_usd": jev, "openai_usd": openai,

    if cold is not None:
        result["cold"] = cold
    (directory / "results").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (directory / "results" / f"{run_id}.json").write_text(json.dumps(result))


def _stored_run(store, run_id, prs, items, cold=False):
    store.create_run(run_id, "o/r", "2026-10")
    for n, data in items.items():
        store.save_item(run_id, n, "done", "pay", data)
    store.finish_run(run_id, "proposed", {"repo": "o/r", "cold": cold, "cost": {
        "prs": prs, "jev_usd": 0.001, "openai_usd": 0.0, "pr_seconds": 4.0}})

def test_sandbox_runs_count_each_oracle_build_once():
    items = {1: {"data": {"oracle": ORACLE, "verification": {"runs": [{}, {}]}}},
             2: {"data": {"oracle": ORACLE, "verification": {"runs": [{}]}}},
             3: {"data": {}}}
    assert economics.sandbox_runs(items) == 2 + 1 + 2

    _eval_result(evals_dir, "cold-1", 10, 0.001, 0.010, 2.0)
    _eval_result(evals_dir, "cold-2", 10, 0.003, 0.010, 4.0, cold=True)
    _eval_result(evals_dir, "old", 10, 0.001, None, 2.0)  # from before OpenAI dollars were tracked
    store = Store(tmp_path / "linus.db")
    _stored_run(store, "warm", 2, {1: {"oracle": ORACLE, "verification": {"runs": [{}, {}]}},
                                   2: {"verification": {"runs": [{}]}}})

    result = economics.build(evals_dir, store, 49, 0.005, 10)
    m = result["measured"]
    assert m["basis"] == "cold runs" and m["cold_runs_used"] == 2 and m["prs_measured"] == 20
    assert m["jev_usd_per_pr"] == pytest.approx(0.0002)
    assert m["openai_usd_per_pr"] == pytest.approx(0.001)
    assert m["model_usd_per_pr"] == pytest.approx(0.0012)
    assert m["jev_usd_per_run"] == pytest.approx(0.002) and m["openai_usd_per_run"] == pytest.approx(0.01)
    assert m["agent_seconds_per_pr"] == pytest.approx(3.0)

    warm = next(r for r in result["runs"] if r["run_id"] == "warm")
    assert warm["from"] == "store" and warm["cold"] is False

    assert row["agent_hours"] == pytest.approx(3000 / 3600, abs=0.01) and row["sandbox_runs"] == 2500

| `uv run linus receipt <file>` | Re-runs a receipt's sandbox proof, no LLM calls, and compares |

| `uv run linus demo --publish OWNER/REPO` | Publishes the demo month as a public GitHub repo with real PRs |
| `uv run linus close --github OWNER/REPO` | Runs the close on a GitHub repo's PRs (`--period YYYY-MM`, default this UTC month) |
| `uv run linus close --github OWNER/REPO --comment` | Same, then posts every verdict on its PR, labels it, and updates a "Bounty close" issue |
| `uv run linus eval --github OWNER/REPO --demo-authors` | Cold run on the published demo, scored against ground truth |
| `uv run linus economics` | Measured cost per run and per PR, plus projections; writes `economics.json` and `economics.csv` |

Rules for the pool live in [`bounty.yml`](bounty.yml): budget per currency,
point table, cap, minimum payout, duplicate threshold, excluded authors.

## On GitHub

Linus reads a real repository with `--github OWNER/REPO`. It only reads unless
you pass `--comment`: issues with a bounty label and the month's PRs come from
the REST API, and the code from a clone in `.linus/github/` that also fetches
every PR's head (`refs/pull/*/head`), so PRs from forks work. Without
`--github` everything runs on the local demo month as before.

The demo month can be published as a live public repo:

```bash
uv run linus demo --publish OWNER/REPO                         # repo, labels, 5 issues, 13 PRs
uv run linus close --github OWNER/REPO --demo-authors --comment
uv run linus approve <run>                                     # also marks the close issue approved
```

`--publish` creates the repo under your account if it doesn't exist, pushes
`main` (with a README explaining the demo) and every PR branch with your own
git credentials, creates the `bounty` and `linus: pay|reject|flag` labels,
opens the 5 issues in order and the 13 PRs in their original order. Running it
again skips everything that already exists; it refuses to overwrite a `main`
that differs from the demo's unless you pass `--force`. All 13 PRs are opened
by your account, so `--demo-authors` takes each contributor's name from the
head commit's author instead (on a real repo, leave it off: commit authors are
whatever the contributor typed). Anyone can open a PR against a bounty issue to
try to fool it; it is judged at the next close.

With `--comment`, after the close has finished (proposed or halted), each PR
gets one comment that is updated on later runs: the verdict and reason, the
evidence (reproduction test on base and on the PR, the suite result, JEV
signals with probabilities, deleted tests or harness edits), points and
proposed payout, the receipt hash, run id and neatlogs trace id. Each PR gets
exactly one `linus:` label, and one "Bounty close YYYY-MM" issue carries the
leaderboard, every verdict, the invariants and the model cost per PR. GitHub
writes happen after the close, never inside it, and GitHub errors are logged
and skipped, so an outage can't break or change a close.

All four pieces are built and in one commit (`4521934`), not pushed. `uv run pytest -q tests` passes all 126 tests with no network. The tests use an in-memory GitHub API on httpx's MockTransport, plus local bare git repos standing in as the GitHub remote. I didn't run `eval`, `close` or `demo --publish` against GitHub, so nothing has been tried on real GitHub yet; your first publish is the real test.

**What's new**
- **`src/linus/github.py`**: all GitHub HTTP goes through this client. It sends the two required headers, makes 3 attempts with backoff, waits out 403/429 rate limits (up to 2 minutes, then fails) and follows pagination. `linus doctor` uses it too.
- **`linus demo --publish OWNER/REPO`** (`publish.py`): creates the repo, pushes `main` and the PR branches with git, creates the labels, then opens the 5 issues and the 13 PRs in order. Running it again skips anything that already exists.
- **`GitHubSource`** in `source.py`, used by `linus close --github …` and `linus eval --github … --demo-authors`. Without `--github`, everything behaves as before.
- **`--comment`** (`github_report.py`): runs after the close finishes, never inside the per-PR loop. GitHub errors are logged and skipped. It only edits comments and issues posted by the token's own account, so another user can't plant a fake marker comment and have Linus overwrite it. `linus approve` updates the close issue if one exists.
- **`linus economics`**: on your local data, 4 cold runs (48 PRs) give a measured model cost of **$0.00092 per PR** ($0.000059 JEV + $0.000864 OpenAI). That's 2.35 agent-seconds and 1.78 sandbox runs per PR. With the default assumptions, gross margin is 97% at 100 PRs/month and 71% at 1,000. At 10,000 it goes negative (about −190%), because $49 per repo doesn't cover that volume. That's worth knowing before the cfo.ai model. I deleted the `economics.json` and `economics.csv` my test run produced, so they aren't committed.

**Decisions you may want to revisit**
- **`--force` on `demo`:** that flag already meant "rebuild". It still does by default; together with `--publish` it means "overwrite a remote `main` that differs".
- **Demo README on `main` only:** it's added as an extra commit on the remote `main` without touching your local demo repo. The demo build is deterministic, so publishing again produces the same commit.
- **Issue numbers:** if the target repo already has issues, the new ones won't be #1–#5. In that case `--publish` rewrites "Fixes #N" in the PR bodies so the links still point at the right issues.
- **Projection basis:** the table is per repo: one repo with N PRs a month, priced at `--price-per-repo`. No other assumptions were added.
- **Small additions:**
  - `linus receipt` now also works on receipts from GitHub runs.
  - A close now fetches its PRs before it creates the run, so a GitHub outage doesn't leave an empty run behind.
  - Run summaries now record the source, whether the run was cold, and each PR's branch.
- **README limitations:** I replaced "GitHub source is next" with an honest one: Linus runs when you start a close, not when a PR arrives.

**One thing to check on the first publish:** issues are created with their fixture labels (`bounty` plus `bug`). New GitHub repos have a `bug` label by default, but I haven't confirmed GitHub's behaviour if it's missing.

To try it: `uv run linus demo --publish OWNER/REPO`, then `uv run linus close --github OWNER/REPO --demo-authors --comment`.
